stem:
Meera lowers a metal bucket into the well at her grandmother's house in Kerala. She notices that the bucket feels much lighter while it is under water than when she lifts it out into the air.

Which statement correctly explains why the immersed bucket feels lighter?

options.text: The water removes the force of gravity acting on the bucket, so there is no downward force on it.
The water applies an upward force on the bucket, equal to the weight of water it displaces, while gravity still pulls it down.
The bucket's mass decreases while it is immersed, so it weighs less under water.
The water pushes down on the top of the bucket harder than it pushes up from below.

teacher.key_rationale: An immersed object experiences an upward buoyant force from the liquid equal to the weight of liquid displaced, while the Earth's pull still acts; the net effect is that the object feels lighter. Only option B states this correctly. A is wrong because gravity is not removed; C is wrong because mass does not change on immersion; D is wrong because pressure increases with depth, so the upward push from below is greater.
